plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 30% of the book, to favor income and broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target of ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and concentrating on income and broad market exposure. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%, MUU to 3%, and METU to 2% to reduce overall leverage.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Buy MSFT at 4% to add exposure to a high-quality tech name from the scanner.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some tech exposure with reduced leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech. Expect moderate returns with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to SOXL, MUU, METU, and SPAL, increasing exposure to leveraged ETFs within limits.
Buy MSFT at 6% to add exposure to a high-scoring tech setup.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth, using strict stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretch growth by using and adding leveraged ETFs and concentrating in high-scoring setups. This approach significantly raises both potential upside and drawdown. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can lose a lot fast; strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 30% of the book, to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on parking cash for yield and low drawdown, not growth.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions and low drawdown. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index, cutting leverage and high-beta names. Distributions are variable and NAV can still fall; this is cash-like income, not a savings account.
